title: Type 1 and type 2 hypervisors: the difference that matters

videos.script: Every hypervisor does the same job. It shares one computer out among several guests. {{job}} They differ in where they sit. Some run as an application on a system you already have, like any other program. That is type 2. {{type2}} Others are the first thing the computer boots. There is no ordinary system under them, and everything else runs on top as a guest. That is type 1. {{type1}} The labels matter less than one question: who is closest to the hardware. The answer decides speed, and who a guest has to ask for anything. {{closest}} There is also a second question, and it matters more for speed. Does the processor help? Modern processors have features made for this, called VT-x on Intel and AMD-V on AMD. {{help}} The computer this course was recorded on does not get those features. You will see what that costs: the same small program, on the host and in a guest, and a stopwatch. {{stopwatch}}
